meta.title: Operation of Reflux Setup in Pharmaceutical Chemistry Laboratory

sections.purpose: To heat reaction mixtures at or above the boiling point of the solvent for extended periods without solvent loss, enabling completion of organic synthesis reactions that require prolonged heating.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmaceutical Chemistry laboratory for organic synthesis reactions including esterification, amide bond formation, condensation reactions, and preparation of pharmaceutical intermediates.
procedure: Choose the correct round-bottom flask size — fill to no more than 2/3 capacity.
Add all reactants and solvent to the flask; add boiling chips or a magnetic stir bar.
Mount the flask securely in a heating mantle or on a water bath using an appropriate flask support.
Attach a Liebig condenser vertically above the flask using a rubber bung or B24 ground glass joint.
Connect the cold water supply to the condenser lower inlet; outlet at the top.
Confirm steady coolant water flow before applying heat.
Attach a drying tube (calcium chloride or silica gel) to the top of the condenser if the reaction is moisture-sensitive.
Begin heating slowly — gradually increase heating mantle voltage or water bath temperature.
Once reflux begins, adjust heating to maintain a steady reflux rate — solvent condensing dripping back 1–2 drops/second at the base of the condenser is the target.
If using a magnetic stirrer, maintain slow stirring throughout for uniform temperature.
Monitor the reaction mixture for colour change, precipitation, or clarification as indicators of reaction progress.
Maintain reflux for the specified reaction time (per protocol).
After the reaction time, reduce heat to zero; allow to cool to room temperature naturally.
Stop the coolant water only after the flask has cooled to room temperature.
Disassemble, collect the reaction mixture, and proceed to workup and isolation steps.
Record: reactants, volumes, solvent, temperature, duration, observations, and yield in the laboratory notebook.
precautions: Always start coolant water flow before applying heat — without coolant, vapours escape from the top of the condenser and create fire risk.
Use boiling chips in every reflux — smooth boiling prevents dangerous bumping.
Never heat a completely sealed apparatus — pressure buildup causes explosion.
Do not add flammable solvents to an already hot flask — add all solvents at room temperature.
Use a heating mantle or water/sand bath — never an open flame with organic solvents.
Work in a fume hood for all reflux involving volatile organic solvents.
Inspect all glassware joints before use — cracked joints leak solvent vapour.
Do not leave reflux unattended if coolant supply may fail.
